proposals.hypothesis: LiAlSiO4 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating aluminosilicate with fully oxidized Al3+ and a silicate framework that should resist oxidation at 4.0 V vs LiCoO2. Its Al3+ gives less driving force for La/Zr reduction than the Zr- or Ta-based products that dominated earlier contact penalties. Compared with Li3AlSiO5 and Li5Al(SiO4)2, it has a lower Li content, which may reduce the self-decomposition penalty seen in the Li-rich silicates (0.13 and 0.086).
proposals.motivation: Li5Al(SiO4)2 (contact 0.050, self-decomposition 0.086) and Li3AlSiO5 (contact 0.038, self-decomposition 0.135) showed that Al-silicate chemistry gives the lowest contact penalties after the LiAlO2 polymorphs. This tests a different Li/Al/Si ratio within that family.

proposal.hypothesis: Li3PO4 is a wide-gap (well above 2 eV), electronically insulating lithium phosphate. It is chemically compatible with LLZO and is known as an effective ion-conducting interlayer on cathodes. Its phosphate anion is hard to oxidize, so it should resist decomposition at 4.0 V against LiCoO2 and is unlikely to react strongly with LLZO at equilibrium, keeping the interfacial penalty low.

Li2ZrO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-rich oxide. Because it shares Zr and Li with LLZO, it should have little driving force to react with the garnet at equilibrium, and its oxide anion is stable against oxidation at 4.0 V vs LiCoO2. This is a different chemical family from the phosphate tried earlier, aiming to lower the contact reaction penalty below the Li3PO4 result, which formed LaPO4 and ZrO2 at about 0.099 eV per non-Li atom.
proposal.motivation: Earlier Li3PO4 contact with LLZO gave penalty 0.099 eV/non-Li atom (bin 4, not acceptable) from LaPO4/ZrO2 formation, so a different family with shared Zr and high Li content is proposed.

proposal.hypothesis: LiAlO2 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating lithium oxide with Al3+ in a fully oxidized, highly stable octahedral/tetrahedral framework. It resists oxidation at 4.0 V vs LiCoO2 and is a well-known cathode coating. Al3+ is a weaker driving force for La/Zr reduction than the Zr4+ in Li2ZrO3, so it should give a lower contact penalty with LLZO than the earlier Li2ZrO3 (penalty 0.30) and may avoid the LaPO4 formation seen with Li3PO4 (penalty 0.099).
proposal.motivation: Li2ZrO3 gave a high self-decomposition penalty (0.30, bin 14) and Li3PO4 gave a contact penalty of 0.099 (bin 4) from LaPO4/ZrO2 formation. A different, oxidation-stable Li-M-O family with a non-Zr cation is needed to lower both.

proposal.hypothesis: LiTaO3 is a wide-gap, electronically insulating Li-M-O oxide with Ta5+, a fully oxidized and highly stable cation that should resist oxidation at 4.0 V vs LiCoO2. Ta5+ is similar in size and charge environment to Zr4+, so it may be chemically compatible with LLZO, avoiding the La-phosphate and La-zirconate reduction products seen with Li3PO4 and LiAlO2.
